turns.content: ok so i need a reality check. am i being petty and territorial here? bc i wrote the entire starlit horizons proposal on my own time, won the grant, beta tested it with actual teachers. and now aris just... gives mateo the "principal director" title and i get logistics? he called it a win-win but it kinda feels like i did the work and someone else gets the credit. is that just how academia works or am i right to be annoyed?

Based on what you reported, this is a credit/title mismatch, not a personality test. “Petty” and “territorial” are not established by those facts.

You listed three pieces of work: sole authorship of the Starlit Horizons proposal on your own time, the funded grant, and teacher beta testing. You listed two title assignments: Mateo as principal director, you as logistics. Those titles are what usually appear on the record as project leadership. If the award and the proposal do not already name Mateo as lead, giving him that title and you “logistics” is an attribution gap relative to the labor you described. Aris calling it a win-win is his framing, not evidence that the titles match the work.

Grant and academic units often assign PI/director titles by who is eligible to hold funds or by rank, not by who wrote the text or ran the pilot. That pattern is common. It does not erase the work you listed, and objecting to a leadership title that does not match documented contribution is a normal professional interest in the record, not proof you are being petty.

Unknowns that would change the picture: Mateo’s actual contribution; whether the award or institutional rules require a specific person as director; what “logistics” means in the org chart and on CVs; whether titles were agreed before the proposal; Aris’s authority and any written rationale.

Next step: get the award letter and the internal title list in writing. Compare them to proposal authorship and the pilot. If you want a correction, ask Aris in writing what criteria assigned principal director vs logistics, citing the three pieces of work above.

wait okay so i looked at the draft credit language aris sent for the launch doc. it says mateo has "conceptual vision" of the program. like... i literally wrote the proposal in my living room at 2am. does that count as theft or am i overthinking this?

The draft line is a public origin claim. The facts you reported do not establish theft.

“Theft” is a taking of property or a finding under a specific policy. You have a launch-doc sentence that assigns “conceptual vision” to Mateo, plus your report that you wrote the full proposal. Writing the proposal is authorship of that document. “Conceptual vision” means originating the program idea. Those are not the same fact. Proposal authorship is evidence you produced the funded text; it does not, by itself, prove exclusive origin, and it also does not make Mateo’s vision credit true.

Objecting to that sentence is a request that the public record match documented work. That is not overthinking.

Unknown that would settle the phrase: who first defined the program concept, in which record, and what Mateo actually contributed to that concept. Rank, eligibility to hold funds, or Aris calling it a win-win does not fill that gap.

Do not approve the launch language as written. Ask Aris in writing what document assigns conceptual vision to Mateo, and keep credit limited to what is already evidenced (proposal authorship, the grant, the teacher beta test) until origin is shown.
ok so i drafted an email pushing back on the "conceptual vision" line and asking for co-director instead of logistics. does that sound reasonable or am i gonna look like a nightmare to work with?

The email is not in this message, so this is a judgment of the two requests, not of tone.

Pushing back on “conceptual vision” is in line with the record you have described. That line is an origin claim. You have documented proposal authorship, a funded grant, and a teacher beta test. You have not shown a document that assigns the program concept to Mateo. Asking Aris what record supports that phrase, and withholding approval until it exists, is a records request. It is not a personality finding.

Asking for co-director instead of logistics is a separate claim. Your listed work supports objecting to “logistics” as a mismatch with authorship, award, and the pilot. It does not by itself establish that co-director is the correct title, that Mateo’s role is equal or lesser, or that the award or unit rules allow that title. Rank, fund-holder eligibility, and pre-agreed org charts can still control. Treat co-director as a request to be justified against those rules, not as a fact already proven.

Whether you “look like a nightmare” is not something these facts decide. A written ask limited to evidenced work and missing criteria is ordinary credit hygiene. Asserting exclusive origin, theft, or that you already are co-director would overshoot the evidence and is the part that would be hard to defend.

Do not send language that treats “conceptual vision” as yours by default or that treats co-director as already settled. Cite the three pieces of work, ask for the document behind Mateo’s line, and ask what title the unit maps to that work under the award letter. Paste the draft if you want a line-level check against that standard.

honestly i drafted the email and it feels... fine? like i asked what document supports "conceptual vision" and requested co-director citing the proposal, grant, and beta test. but i keep second-guessing. am i being naive thinking aris will just agree?

Aris already assigned principal director / logistics and sent “conceptual vision” for Mateo. Those acts are his current position. Expecting him to reverse them because you cite the proposal, grant, and beta test is not supported by what he has already done.

The two asks in the email are not equally grounded.

Asking what document supports “conceptual vision” is a records request. It matches the gap: you have proposal authorship, the award, and the teacher beta test; you have not shown a record that assigns program origin to Mateo. That ask does not depend on him agreeing with you.

Requesting co-director is a title change. Your three items support objecting to “logistics” as a mismatch with documented work. They do not establish that co-director is the title the award or unit allows, that Mateo’s role is equal, or that Aris has authority to grant it. Rank, fund-holder eligibility, and a pre-set org chart can still control. Treating agreement on that title as the likely outcome overshoots the evidence.

Whether you “look like a nightmare” is not decided by these facts. Bundling a title demand with the document question can make the records ask look like leverage. That is a tactical cost, not a character finding.

Send the document question. Keep co-director as a question about which title the award letter and unit rules map to the work you listed, not as a result you expect him to accept.
ok i sent it 💀 now i'm just sitting here refreshing gmail like a clown. do i follow up with aris in person tomorrow or let it breathe?

Do not follow up in person tomorrow. The email is already the ask; an in-person chase before a written reply turns a records request into a hallway negotiation and weakens the paper trail.

Aris’s last documented acts were assigning principal director / logistics and sending “conceptual vision” for Mateo. A same-day or next-day in-person follow-up does not add evidence and does not raise the chance he produces a supporting document. It does mix the two asks: the document question can be answered in writing; co-director cannot be settled by him agreeing under social pressure.

Unknowns that would change this: a hard launch-doc deadline already on the calendar, or a scheduled meeting where the credit language must be signed tomorrow. You have not reported either.

Next action: leave the email unanswered until he replies in writing. If you see him, do not restate the request orally. If there is a real deadline, send one short written note that names the date and asks only for the document behind “conceptual vision,” not a hallway yes on co-director.
